state.project: Moneta: a memory substrate for AI agents. v1 is shipped and locked by a spec that can only change through a formal escalation round. v5 is a working reference implementation beside v1 that changes four locked decisions; nothing flips until the owner rules.
v5_principles: The journal is the database: every change is one checksummed, fsync'd line appended to one file; records, the vector index and USD layers are derived by folding it.
Reads are pure: a read is a function of the journal prefix, the policy, the context and the evaluation time, and never writes.
Records don't compose; policy does.
facts: In v1, a deposit is lost on restart unless a sleep pass ran, because the snapshot is only written in the sleep pass.
In v1, query() mutates utility and last-evaluated time on every read.
v1's locked spec sets LastEvaluated = now at attention write and then evaluates decay after it, which erases the decay since the last read. The code does what the spec says.
v1's attention log is lock-free only because of the CPython GIL; it refuses to run on free-threaded Python.
In v1, prune physically deletes a memory and reports only a count.
The first host, SYNAPSE, carries about 1,300 lines compensating for these behaviors, including snapshotting the whole store on every add.
v5 passes its own 124 tests plus all of v1's, and 247 of SYNAPSE's 253 Moneta tests unchanged; the 6 failures assert v1 data loss.
Measured on one machine at 10,000 records: making one deposit durable takes 3.26 s in v1's snapshot pattern and 0.43 ms as one v5 journal append.
v5 has not yet run against a copy of a real 841-record SYNAPSE store.
The owner is a solo developer on a fixed budget. A later design (v6/v7) assumes all four v5 changes and the half-life call.

e1_authority.instructions: Given `v5_principles` and `facts`, which structure should be authoritative for what memories exist?

journal_authoritative.what: The fsync'd journal comes first and is the authority; the vector index and USD are derived and rebuildable.
journal_authoritative.best_case: Memory survives process death by construction; one truth, so no split brain.
journal_authoritative.cost: Overturns a locked decision (USD first, vector index authoritative) and changes the storage format.

vector_index_authoritative.what: Keep v1: USD is written first, then the in-memory vector index, which is the authority for existence.
vector_index_authoritative.best_case: No change to the locked spec or to existing stores.
vector_index_authoritative.cost: The authority does not survive process death unless a snapshot was taken.

e2_decay_evaluation.instructions: Given `v5_principles` and `facts`, how should decay be evaluated? The decay formula itself is unchanged either way.

pure_evaluation.what: Decay is a pure function of the anchor and the time, evaluated anywhere; reads never write; attention is applied at its own timestamp.
pure_evaluation.best_case: Same inputs give the same answer, so every read can be replayed; fixes the decay erased by the spec order.
pure_evaluation.cost: Replaces the locked rule of exactly three mutation points.

three_mutation_points.what: Keep v1: decay mutates stored utility at exactly three evaluation points, including on every query.
three_mutation_points.best_case: No change to the locked spec.
three_mutation_points.cost: Reads write state, and the specified order erases decay since the last read.

e3_concurrency.instructions: Given `v5_principles` and `facts`, what should order concurrent writes?

single_ordered_journal.what: One append-only journal for every write, ordered by a single writer lock with a gap-free sequence number; attention is visible immediately.
single_ordered_journal.best_case: Correctness no longer depends on the GIL; live state equals replay.
single_ordered_journal.cost: Replaces the locked lock-free attention log; attention becomes visible at once instead of at the next sleep pass.

gil_attention_log.what: Keep v1: a lock-free append-only attention log reduced at the sleep pass, relying on the CPython GIL.
gil_attention_log.best_case: No change to the locked spec; no writer lock on the attention path.
gil_attention_log.cost: Refuses free-threaded Python; attention is invisible until the next sleep pass.

h_half_life_change.instructions: Given `v5_principles` and `facts`, when the owner changes the decay half-life, what should happen to history?

reinterpret_history.what: Utility anchors are recomputed on replay with the current half-life, deterministically; each change is noted in the journal.
reinterpret_history.best_case: One consistent decay rate over all history; replay stays deterministic.
reinterpret_history.cost: Past answers change when the half-life changes; a later design needs a separate ranking-only half-life to tune safely.

rate_applies_forward.what: A half-life change applies only from the moment it is made; earlier decay keeps the old rate.
rate_applies_forward.best_case: Past answers never change because of a later setting.
rate_applies_forward.cost: Replay must track a history of rates; more state and more to explain.
